note.text:
Some gases dissolve in liquids: carbon dioxide in a soft drink, oxygen in river water (fish breathe it).
A gas is less soluble when the liquid is warmer or when the pressure falls, so a dissolved gas can be removed by:
• heating the liquid gently: bubbles of gas come out (warm water holds less gas);
• shaking or stirring, or lowering the pressure: when you open a soft drink, the pressure drops and the gas fizzes out.
The gas can be collected over water in a gas jar or test tube.
This is why a soft drink goes “flat” when it is open and warm, and why fish can struggle in water that is too warm.

worked_example.problem: Why does a warm bottle of soft drink fizz more than a cold one when it is opened?
steps: The drink has carbon dioxide dissolved in it under pressure.
Opening the bottle lowers the pressure, so gas comes out.
Warm liquid holds less dissolved gas than cold liquid, so even more gas escapes.
worked_example.answer: Warm liquid holds less gas, so more carbon dioxide escapes when the pressure is released.

cards.idea: Gases can dissolve in liquids: carbon dioxide in a soft drink, oxygen in river water.
example: Fish use the oxygen dissolved in water.

cards.idea: Heating a liquid drives out the dissolved gas: warm water holds less gas.
example: Bubbles appear in water being heated before it boils.

cards.idea: Lowering the pressure or shaking also lets the gas escape.
example: Opening a soft drink: the pressure drops and it fizzes.

check.prompt: Why does a soft drink fizz when the bottle is opened?

right.text: The pressure drops, so the dissolved carbon dioxide comes out.

wrong.explain: It does not boil; the dissolved gas escapes.
The bubbles are carbon dioxide coming out of the drink.
The gas was already dissolved: it is carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a mixture of a gas dissolved in a liquid?

right.text: river water with oxygen in it

questions.prompt: How can you remove the dissolved gas from a glass of soft drink?

right.text: Warm it gently and stir it.

wrong.explain: Cold liquid holds more gas, not less.
Sugar does not remove the gas.
A filter cannot hold back a dissolved gas.

questions.prompt: In the dry season, a fish pond becomes very warm. Why can this harm the fish?

right.text: Warm water holds less dissolved oxygen, so the fish have less to breathe.

wrong.text: Warm water has more oxygen, which is poisonous.
wrong.explain: Warm water holds less oxygen, not more.
The main problem is less dissolved oxygen.

wrong.text: Warm water turns into carbon dioxide.
wrong.explain: Water does not turn into carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

right.text: Opening a soft drink lowers the pressure.
Fish breathe oxygen dissolved in water.
A dissolved gas can be collected over water.
Warm water holds less dissolved gas than cold water.

wrong.text: Cold water holds less dissolved gas than warm water.
wrong.explain: It is the other way round: cold water holds more gas.

wrong.text: Filtering removes dissolved gas from a drink.
wrong.explain: A filter cannot stop a dissolved gas.
